non_blocking: No paper found that contains the main result (pooled pick-or-NONE vs isolated verification on all-wrong pools, with a select-then-verify effect). No ABANDON basis.

Closest unlisted prior work worth citing: arXiv:2409.04168 (Stephan et al.) finds LLM judges 'tend to favor higher-quality models even if their answer is incorrect' on math, a nearby precedent for judge-favoured wrong candidates.

arXiv:2610.08153 (kim2026penalty, cited) abstract: models still produce invalid forced-choice responses when the correct option is removed; the paper cites it only in the A4 section as 'studies abstention when no option is valid'. It is closer to the target-absent premise than the related-work paragraph credits; the novelty sentence should be scoped against it, since it already shows forced choice on option sets with no valid answer.

arXiv:2503.01550 (tam2025none) abstract: NA-correct items cause 30-50% drops, 'LLMs lack the meta-cognitive ability to systematically evaluate and reject all given options when none are correct'. Accurately characterised in the paper.

Related-work characterisations checked and accurate: ji2026candidate (arXiv:2608.25937) does exclude all-wrong pools ('All-wrong pools were excluded', Fig 4c; mixed-pool rank AUC); wang2025llms abstract confirms 'selecting the least incorrect option'; tam2025none correct. The detailed wang2025llms confidence and replaced-option claims (paper line 34) could not be verified from the abstract alone and need full-text confirmation by the citation auditor.
zhang2026selected is cited from its abstract only (the paper discloses this).
The eyewitness-to-LLM framing returned no direct prior LLM work in my searches, but search coverage of 2026 preprints is imperfect; novelty is therefore reasonably but not conclusively established.
